stem.en: Nobody wrote down the journey out of Africa. What is the main evidence that Homo erectus spread into Asia and Europe?

text.en: Paintings in African caves show maps of the route.

feedback.en: No such maps exist. The evidence for this journey is stone tools, not pictures.

text.en: Handaxes and cleavers have been found in other parts of Asia and in Europe.
Skeletons lie one after another along the whole route.

feedback.en: Fossils are rare, and nothing like an unbroken line of skeletons has been found.

text.en: Neanderthals in Europe made flake tools, and that shows Homo erectus left Africa.

feedback.en: Those are Middle Palaeolithic tools made by a different species, so they say nothing about Homo erectus leaving Africa.

explanation.en: Homo erectus is linked with handaxes and cleavers. Finding such tools in Asia and Europe points to tools that began in Africa and spread beyond it, between about 2 and 0.5 million years ago.

hints.en: What did these people leave behind that could last for two million years?
